summary: The original runner completed only the n0.17m, n1.1m and n3.7m arms before its obsolete quality-gate branch exited. The three retained observations use radically different optimizer-step budgets, so they are useful optimization-budget diagnostics but cannot answer the intended five-scale quality question. The missing n8.6m and n16.6m arms were not started under this experiment; CR-TOK-0003 supersedes it with 20,000 updates for every scale.

comparisons.name: n1p1m_minus_n0p17m_ema_clean_psnr_db
comparisons.interpretation_limit: Capacity and optimizer-step allocation both differ, so this is not a controlled capacity effect.

comparisons.name: n3p7m_online_minus_ema_clean_psnr_db
comparisons.interpretation_limit: The large online-versus-EMA gap after only 2,938 updates is evidence of an immature endpoint, not proof that more updates must improve every held-out metric.

deviations.before: Train n8.6m and n16.6m only when smaller candidates miss an absolute quality gate.
deviations.after: Train n0.17m, n1.1m, n3.7m, n8.6m and n16.6m unconditionally; use metrics only for post-hoc comparison and ranking.
deviations.bias_control: The amendment occurred during fresh n0.17m training before any held-out evaluation existed, so no observed scale result selected the new rule.

deviations.before: Use per-scale FLOPs budgets, which produced 62,675 / 9,358 / 2,938 / 2,550 / 2,656 allocated optimizer steps.
deviations.after: Preserve this run as an incomplete optimization-budget diagnostic and start a new five-scale experiment with exactly 20,000 optimizer updates per arm.
deviations.bias_control: The new experiment receives a new ID because training budget is a comparison-defining variable. Existing checkpoints and metrics remain immutable.

observed: Fresh n0.17m, n1.1m and n3.7m arms completed 62,675, 9,358 and 2,938 updates respectively; n8.6m and n16.6m did not run under this experiment.
On the identical 512 held-out clips, EMA clean PSNR was 12.0621 dB for n0.17m, 27.2563 dB for n1.1m and 26.2075 dB for n3.7m.
At n3.7m, online clean PSNR was 29.3045 dB while EMA clean PSNR was 26.2075 dB after only 2,938 updates.
interpretation: The run demonstrates that the representation is no longer universally collapsed at n1.1m, but the unequal update budgets confound capacity with optimization maturity.
The n3.7m online-versus-EMA gap makes its short endpoint especially unsuitable for selecting the best attainable tokenizer.
not_established: Which tokenizer scale is visually acceptable.
Whether quality improves monotonically with capacity at a comparable optimization horizon.
Whether any tokenizer candidate can support a controllable dynamics model.
decision: Do not run the missing two arms under this mixed-budget protocol.
Run CR-TOK-0003 with 20,000 updates for all five scales and evaluate 2,500, 5,000, 10,000 and 20,000-update milestones.
Keep dynamics blocked until the fixed-20k comparison receives explicit visual acceptance.
